q.intro.text: A garden bed is four feet wide. Along its length there are x feet of tomatoes, then three feet of herbs.

q.ask.text: Its area is four times the quantity x plus three, in square feet. Which expression has the same value, for every length x?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the algebra.

e.s1.text: Each row is one strip, x long, and three squares. Four rows make the bed: four groups of x plus three.

e.s2.text: Split the bed where the tomatoes end. Both parts are still four rows high: four times x, and four times three.

e.s3.text: The strips make four x. The squares make twelve: four rows of three, not just three.

e.s4.text: Four times the quantity x plus three is four x plus twelve, for every x. That's the distributive property. Read it backwards, and you have factored four x plus twelve.

e.why.text: Quick check. Why is it plus twelve, and not plus three?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. The four multiplies every term inside the parentheses: each of the four rows has three squares.

e.w-part.text: Then only the top row would have squares. Look: all four rows have three squares, so twelve.

e.w-pemdas.text: PEMDAS says what to do first. It does not explain the twelve. The rows do: four rows of three squares.

t.intro.text: Now the bed is three rows of two x plus five. The first two steps are done for you.

t.area.text: Your step. Find the area of each part, and write three times the quantity two x plus five as a sum.

t.a-ok.text: Yes. Three rows of two strips make six x, and three rows of five squares make fifteen.

t.a-part.text: Count the squares. Each of the three rows has five. That makes fifteen, not five.

t.a-concat.text: Three times two x is six x: three rows of two strips. It is not thirty two x.

t.a-unlike.text: Strips and squares are unlike terms. Six x and fifteen stay separate.

t.a-other.text: Count each part: the strips, three rows of two, and the squares, three rows of five.

t.name.text: Which property turns three times the quantity two x plus five into six x plus fifteen?

t.n-ok.text: Yes, the distributive property. The three is shared out to every term inside.

t.n-comm.text: The commutative property changes the order, and nothing was reordered here. The three went into the sum.

t.n-assoc.text: The associative property moves parentheses. Here, a factor went into a sum.

t.back.text: Now read it backwards. Six x plus fifteen is what number times the quantity two x plus five?

t.b-ok.text: Yes, three. The parts slide back together. That is factoring.

t.b-one.text: Check it. Six times five is thirty, not fifteen. The factor has to go into both terms.

t.b-other.text: Which number times two x makes six x, and times five makes fifteen?

t.num.text: Type a number in the box.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked four x plus twelve, and you were right. Now you can show why.

t.cb-part.text: At the start you picked four x plus three. The squares show why it is twelve: four rows of three.

t.cb-unlike.text: At the start you picked sixteen x. But four x and twelve are unlike terms. They cannot become one term.

p.intro.text: Riley says two times the quantity x plus three, and three x plus four, are equivalent. I tried x equals two, and both give ten.

p.build.text: Prove it. Fill each because, with the reason that makes the line true.

p.test.text: Let's test that. Build the argument, and see where it leads.

p.c1.text: Right. Two times the quantity x plus three is two x plus six, for every x.

p.c2.text: At x equals zero, two times the quantity x plus three is six, but three x plus four is four. They differ.

p.c3.text: So they are not equivalent. Matching at x equals two was a coincidence.

p.done.text: That is a proof. Every line has its reason, and one counterexample settles it.

p.w-pemdas.text: PEMDAS says what to do first. It does not allow a rewrite. The distributive property does.

p.w-examples.text: That is Riley's slip. Matching at one value is not matching at every value.

p.w-exception.text: A counterexample is not an exception. Equivalent means equal for every x, so one miss breaks it.

p.w-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?
